title: sre-oncall-scratchpad-samir-2026-03-12
content:
On-call scratchpad — 2026-03-12 (Samir Patel)

Purpose: quick personal log for the shift. Raw notes, hypotheses, follow-ups, and TODOs for later handoff. Not polished.

Pager timeline (local times):
- 00:23 — Pager: upstream model-serving 503s for region us-west-2 (alerts aggregated). Brief spike, auto-retry mitigated for some customers.
- 00:27 — Second alert: increased error rate on endpoint /v1/chat/generate (p50 latency x2). Started manual investigation.
- 00:34 — Identified partial OOM on a single dedicated pod (dedicated-gpu-12) causing transient connection resets. Pod restarted by k8s, but requests were queued and retried, increasing latency.
- 00:50 — Applied temporary routing override to route traffic away from the failing pod pool -> immediate drop in errors. Notified Infra and Serving team.
- 01:10 — Postmortem stub created in JIRA (INF-4287). Assigned to: Ava Nguyen for kernel/driver follow-up, Jordan Lee for autoscaler investigation.

Notes from triage:
- Root cause hypothesis: intermittent GPU OOMs during a model compilation path triggered by new sequence length distribution from a customer workload. The affected pod repeatedly failed during KV-cache allocation.
- Evidence: node-exporter logs show memory spike on GPU device 1, dmesg shows user-space OOM messages. Serving logs show repeated compilation/reload attempts for model "open-large-v2-quant" around 00:20-00:35.
- Why it mattered: autoscaler policy rebalanced capacity slowly under churn which kept a handful of requests hitting the failing pod pool. Routing fallback wasn't aggressive enough for the failure mode.

Immediate follow-ups (owner / ETA):
- Add a temporary SLO fallback rule to shift traffic to the warm pool if pod restarts > 2 in 5m (Samir) / ETA: by EOD 2026-03-12 (deployed 01:05).
- Investigate compaction/quantization codepath for open-large-v2-quant for higher memory usage (Ava Nguyen) / ETA: 2026-03-17.
- Add a kernel logging hook to capture pre-OOM state (Jordan Lee) / ETA: 2026-03-16.
- Create a replay job for the specific customer traffic pattern to reproduce locally (Samir + Solutions Eng) / ETA: 2026-03-18.

Runbook gaps and TODOs (short-term hacks vs long-term):
- Runbook step for "GPU OOM during compilation" is terse; doesn't cover how to rapidly route traffic away (only mentions pod cordon). TODO: expand with policy examples and kubectl commands. (owner: Samir)
- No automated detection for repeated compilation errors; add a metric "serving.compilation_failures" -> alert if > 5 in 10m. (owner: Jordan)
- Add a clear guidance for rolling back to model-quant variants on failures (docs + console option). Long-term: make fallback automatic. (owner: Product-runbooks)

Communication log (what I posted / who I pinged):
- 00:36 — Posted initial triage in #sre-oncall, pinged @ava and @jordan.
- 00:52 — Updated infra-snapshot in the incident thread with node-exporter graphs and recent pod restarts.
- 01:20 — Sent short note to support-channel to pause escalations for affected customers while we stabilize.

Open questions:
- Did any other customers see degraded quality (not just latency/errors)? Need to check Redwood Optimize traces for quality regressions around this window.
- Is there a correlation with a recent model rollout for open-large-v2-quant? Check model-version tags in request headers.
- Why did autoscaler not pre-provision spare capacity for warm pool? Check scaling policy triggers.

Personal quick TODOs for handoff:
- Draft an expanded runbook section for GPU-compile OOM (include kubectl commands, routing override examples, and a checklist). Mark as: runbook/gpu-oom-during-compile.
- Add unit/regression test to the compilation code to simulate long sequence lengths. (small spike test)
- Follow up with Ava on confirmation whether driver-level change is required.
- Schedule 30-min cross-team sync with Serving + Infra + Product to decide on automatic fallback approach (Samir to propose times).

Cleanup and next steps during on-call recovery window:
- Ensure the temporary routing override has telemetry (p50/p95 latency vs baseline) and remove once autoscaler changes land.
- Bake the replay scenario into the nightly stress job.
- Onboard a check into Redwood Console: per-model compilation error rate visible in model dashboard.

Notes to self (fluffy, scratch):
- Remember: when it's an OOM during compile, pod restarts will look like "flapping" but stack traces point to the same code path. Look for consistent compilation request IDs.
- Keep runbook language action-first ("do X now"), not theory.

Handoff summary (short):
- Incident INF-4287: transient GPU OOMs during model compilation caused increased errors and latency in us-west-2. Temporary routing override applied and stabilized traffic. Follow-ups assigned to Ava (compilation memory), Jordan (autoscaler/metrics), Samir (runbook + replay).

If anything urgent shows up while I'm off shift, escalate to Jordan and reference INF-4287.

-- end of scratchpad --
